claims.text: Boren Avenue & Pike Street had 11 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 0 people killed.
These counts are Boren Avenue & Pike Street's own: the city's record places 277 of the 294 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $753,000 a year.
24% of crashes here were recorded as “motor vehicle struck motorized scooter, front end at angle” crashes, against 2% at the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 0.3 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $113,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 0.2 crashes a year (CMF 4219, the more conservative of the two middle records of 4; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $59,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red; the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for Boren Avenue, East Pike Street, Melrose Avenue, Minor Avenue, Pike Street (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
